Indeed, geopolitical uncertainty and the impact of artificial intelligence are two dominant labor market themes, along with a shrinking labor force that has helped keep the unemployment rate in check.

Despite the various pressures, companies have avoided widespread layoffs. Weekly jobless claims have been in check, and the total layoff pace in 2026 is the slowest in four years, according to outplacement consultants Challenger, Gray & Christmas. The August report is likely to reinforce the view that the labor market is gradually weakening as demonstrated most clearly by slower wage growth. The fall in EPOPs also indicates weakness, although this could be at least partially reversed in August.

There was a decline in all the duration measures of unemployment in July, which ordinarily would be a positive sign, unless it was due to the longer term unemployed dropping out of the labor force. The August data will provide a clearer picture. [...] By Dean Baker
